source: Quiz 2 - Sessions 1-3: Choosing a Model and Thinking Budgets
question: A classmate installs a model on a laptop with no GPU (graphics processing unit) and says the answer crawls out a word at a time, while the same kind of model in a browser feels close to instant. What best explains the gap?

options.text: The local copy has fewer parameters, so it needs more time to reach the same answer.
options.feedback: Fewer parameters means less capability, not more time -- a smaller model is the faster one, all else equal. The gap here is hardware, not model size.

options.text: The hosted copy runs on hardware that produces roughly ten times more tokens per second.
options.feedback: About 5 tokens per second on a bare laptop against roughly 60 from a hosted service is more than an order of magnitude, and you feel every bit of it because generation is sequential. Same architecture, same code -- different hardware doing the arithmetic.

options.text: The browser holds the whole answer back until it is finished, so nothing is genuinely faster.
options.feedback: Hosted interfaces stream tokens as they arrive, which is why you watch text appear. The speed difference you are seeing is real, not a display trick.

options.text: The laptop has to re-encode the entire context before each token, which the server avoids.
options.feedback: Neither one starts over per token -- that is what stored state such as the KV (key/value) cache is for, and it is part of the same software in both places. The laptop is simply doing the arithmetic on slower hardware.
